def-it-finite-strongly-typical-set:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite nonempty alphabet, let $P$ be a probability vector on $\mathcal A$ in the sense of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]], and let $n\ge1$. Write $\operatorname{supp}(P):=\{a\in\mathcal A:P(a)>0\}$. For $a^n=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\mathcal A^n$, its empirical distribution is $\widehat P_{a^n}(a):=n^{-1}|\{t:a_t=a\}|$. For $\delta>0$, define the support-restricted strongly typical set by
$$T_\delta^{(n)}(P):=\{a^n\in\operatorname{supp}(P)^n:|\widehat P_{a^n}(a)-P(a)|\le\delta P(a)\text{ for every }a\text{ with }P(a)>0\}.$$
For a finite joint law $P_{XA}$ and a fixed $x^n$, write $T_\delta^{(n)}(P_{A|X}\mid x^n):=\{a^n:(x^n,a^n)\in T_\delta^{(n)}(P_{XA})\}$. This conditional set is empty if $x^n$ is outside the support of $P_X$. Zero-probability letters are excluded exactly, so no logarithm of zero occurs in likelihood calculations on these sets.
lem-it-finite-type-class-cardinality-bou:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite nonempty alphabet of size $m$, let $n\ge1$, and let $q$ be an attainable empirical distribution with integer counts $n_a=nq(a)$. Its type class $T_q:=\{a^n\in\mathcal A^n:\widehat P_{a^n}=q\}$ satisfies
$$(n+1)^{-m}\exp(nH(q))\le |T_q|\le \exp(nH(q)),$$
where $H(q):=-\sum_{a:q(a)>0}q(a)\ln q(a)$ and $0\ln0:=0$.
lem-it-finite-codebook-covering-selectio:
## Statement

Let $P_{XU}=P_XP_{U|X}$ be a joint law on finite nonempty alphabets, with marginal $P_U$. Fix $\eta>0$. There are typicality tolerances $\delta>0$ and an integer $n_0$ such that, for every $n\ge n_0$, every $x^n\in T_\delta^{(n)}(P_X)$, and every $R>I(X;U)+\eta$, an iid codebook of $M_n=\lceil e^{nR}\rceil$ independent $P_U^{\otimes n}$ words contains a word jointly typical with $x^n$ with probability tending to one uniformly in $x^n$. If the encoder selects the least index with a jointly typical word, then, conditional on a match, its selected word has law $P_U^{\otimes n}$ conditioned on $T_\delta^{(n)}(P_{XU}|x^n)$; conditional on any particular joint type, this law is uniform on the associated conditional type class.
lem-it-finite-random-bin-packing-bound:
## Statement

Fix $k\ge1$, finite alphabets $\mathcal U_1,\ldots,\mathcal U_k,\mathcal S$, and a joint law $P_{U_1\cdots U_kS}$. Generate the source block $S^n$ with any law and, independently of it, generate mutually independent codebooks whose $M_i$ codewords each have law $P_{U_i}^{\otimes n}$. Generate independent uniform bin labels from $[B_i]$ for every codeword, independently of the source and codebooks. Let the selected true indices $L_i$ be functions of the source and codebooks but not the bin labels. A joint-typicality decoder looks for the unique tuple in the received bins whose codewords and $S^n$ are jointly typical for $P_{U_1\cdots U_kS}$. For each nonempty $J\subseteq[k]$, if
$$\sum_{i\in J}\frac1n\ln\frac{M_i}{B_i}<\sum_{i\in J}H(U_i)-H(U_J\mid U_{J^c},S)-\eta$$
for some $\eta>0$, then, writing $E_n$ for the event that the selected true tuple and $S^n$ are jointly typical, the expected number of wrong jointly typical tuples in its received bins, multiplied by $\mathbf1_{E_n}$, tends to zero as $n\to\infty$. Consequently the probability that $E_n$ holds and a wrong jointly typical tuple exists tends to zero. The case of no side information is represented by a singleton $\mathcal S$.
lem-it-finite-selected-codeword-markov-t:
## Statement

Let $P_{XYZ}(x,y,z)=P_{XY}(x,y)P_{Z|X}(z|x)$ be a finite-alphabet Markov law. For every $\epsilon>0$ there are $\delta>0$ and $n_0$ such that the following holds for $n\ge n_0$: if $(x^n,y^n)\in T_\delta^{(n)}(P_{XY})$ and a random $Z^n$ is supported on $T_\delta^{(n)}(P_{Z|X}\mid x^n)$ and, conditional on each joint type of $(x^n,Z^n)$, is uniform on that conditional type class, then
$$\Pr\{(x^n,y^n,Z^n)\in T_\epsilon^{(n)}(P_{XYZ})\}\ge1-\frac{C}{n},$$
where $C<\infty$ depends only on the fixed finite law, alphabets, and $\epsilon$, not on the particular typical source block or conditional type.
def-it-finite-wyner-ziv-code:
## Definition

Let $(X_t,Y_t)_{t\ge1}$ be an IID pair with joint pmf $P_{XY}$ on finite nonempty alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, as the $k=2$ instance of [[def-it-finite-iid-multisource]]. Let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty and $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$ be a finite bounded distortion, with normalized block distortion $d_n$ from [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]].

A length-$n$, $M$-message Wyner-Ziv code consists of a deterministic encoder $f_n:\mathcal X^n\to[M]$ and deterministic decoder $g_n:[M]\times\mathcal Y^n\to\widehat{\mathcal X}^n$. The encoder observes only $X^n$; the decoder observes both the message and $Y^n$. Its rate is $n^{-1}\ln M$ nats per source symbol, and its expected distortion is $\mathbb E[d_n(X^n,g_n(f_n(X^n),Y^n))]$.

A pair $(R,D)$ is operationally achievable if there are increasing blocklengths $n_j\to\infty$ and such codes with $\limsup_j n_j^{-1}\ln M_j\le R$ and $\limsup_j\mathbb E[d_{n_j}]\le D$. Define $R_{\rm WZ}^{\rm op}(D)$ as the infimum of achievable rates.

For a finite auxiliary alphabet $\mathcal U$, a test channel is a stochastic kernel $P_{U|X}$ together with a deterministic map $g:\mathcal Y\times\mathcal U\to\widehat{\mathcal X}$, under the joint law $P_{XYU}=P_{XY}P_{U|X}$. It has $U-X-Y$, expected distortion $\mathbb E[d(X,g(Y,U))]$, and conditional mutual information $I(X;U|Y)$ from [[def-it-finite-conditional-mutual-information]]. Define the single-letter candidate
$$R_{\rm WZ}(D):=\inf_{\substack{\mathcal U\ {\rm finite},\,P_{U|X},\,g\\\mathbb E[d(X,g(Y,U))]\le D}} I(X;U|Y),$$
with value $+\infty$ if the feasible set is empty. This definition alone makes no operational equality claim; the following theorem proves it and the cardinality lemma makes the finite minimum explicit.
def-it-finite-multiterminal-lossy-code:
## Definition

Fix $k\ge2$ and a finite IID source vector $(X_{1,t},\ldots,X_{k,t})_{t\ge1}$ with law $P_{X_1\cdots X_k}$, as in [[def-it-finite-iid-multisource]]. For each $i$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}_i$ be a finite nonempty reproduction alphabet and let $d_i:\mathcal X_i\times\widehat{\mathcal X}_i\to[0,d_{i,\max}]$ be finite and bounded.

A length-$n$ fixed-length multiterminal lossy code consists of separate deterministic encoders
$$f_{i,n}:\mathcal X_i^n\to[M_i]\quad (1\le i\le k)$$
and one deterministic common decoder
$$g_n:\prod_{i=1}^k[M_i]\to\prod_{i=1}^k\widehat{\mathcal X}_i^n.$$
Write $\widehat X_i^n$ for the $i$th reconstruction and define its expected per-letter distortion by $\Delta_{i,n}:=\mathbb E[n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^n d_i(X_{i,t},\widehat X_{i,t})]$. Encoder $i$ has rate $n^{-1}\ln M_i$ nats per source symbol. A vector $(R_1,\ldots,R_k)$ is achievable at distortions $(D_1,\ldots,D_k)$ when there is an increasing sequence of blocklengths with each rate limsup at most $R_i$ and each distortion limsup at most $D_i$. The operational rate-distortion region is the closure of these achievable vectors.
lem-it-wyner-ziv-auxiliary-cardinality-b:
## Statement

Let $P_{XY}$ be a finite joint law, let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$, and let $(U,P_{U|X},g)$ be any finite Wyner-Ziv test channel from [[def-it-finite-wyner-ziv-code]] with expected distortion at most $D$. There is another finite test channel $(U',P_{U'|X},g')$ such that
$$|\mathcal U'|\le|\mathcal X|+1,\qquad \mathbb E[d(X,g'(Y,U'))]=\mathbb E[d(X,g(Y,U))],\qquad I(X;U'|Y)\le I(X;U|Y).$$
Consequently the infimum $R_{\rm WZ}(D)$ in [[def-it-finite-wyner-ziv-code]] is a minimum and it suffices to optimize over $|\mathcal U|\le|\mathcal X|+1$.
lem-it-finite-wyner-ziv-function-convexi:
## Statement

Let $R_{\rm WZ}(D)$, $D_{\min}$, and $D_{\max}$ be as in [[def-it-finite-wyner-ziv-code]]. Then $D_{\min}\le D_{\max}$, $R_{\rm WZ}$ is nonincreasing and convex on $[D_{\min},\infty)$, $R_{\rm WZ}(D)=0$ for $D\ge D_{\max}$, and $R_{\rm WZ}$ is continuous at every feasible distortion, including $D_{\min}$ and $D_{\max}$.
thm-it-berger-tung-finite-multiterminal-:
## Statement

Fix a finite IID $k$-source with $k\ge2$, per-terminal finite reproduction alphabets, and bounded distortions $d_i$ as in [[def-it-finite-multiterminal-lossy-code]]. Choose finite auxiliary alphabets $\mathcal U_i$, product test channels
$$P_{X_1\cdots X_kU_1\cdots U_k}=P_{X_1\cdots X_k}\prod_{i=1}^kP_{U_i|X_i},$$
and deterministic reconstruction maps $g_i:\prod_{j=1}^k\mathcal U_j\to\widehat{\mathcal X}_i$ whose expected distortions are at most $D_i$. For each nonempty $S\subseteq[k]$, write $X_S=(X_i)_{i\in S}$, $U_S=(U_i)_{i\in S}$, and $S^c=[k]\setminus S$; when $S=[k]$, $U_{S^c}$ is a constant singleton. Then every nonnegative rate vector satisfying
$$\sum_{i\in S}R_i\ge I(X_S;U_S|U_{S^c})\qquad\text{for every nonempty }S\subseteq[k]$$
is achievable at distortions $(D_1,\ldots,D_k)$. The convex hull of the union of these finite-auxiliary rate regions, over all such product test channels and reconstruction maps, is the finite-alphabet Berger-Tung inner bound and is achievable. This theorem does not assert that the inner bound is the exact general multiterminal lossy rate region.
thm-it-finite-alphabet-wyner-ziv-rate-di:
## Statement

Let $(X_t,Y_t)_{t\ge1}$ be IID on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$ be a bounded distortion independent of $Y$. With decoder-only side information and the operational convention of [[def-it-finite-wyner-ziv-code]],
$$R_{\rm WZ}^{\rm op}(D)=R_{\rm WZ}(D)=\min_{\substack{|\mathcal U|\le|\mathcal X|+1,\,P_{U|X},\,g:\mathcal Y\times\mathcal U\to\widehat{\mathcal X}\\U-X-Y,\,\mathbb E d(X,g(Y,U))\le D}} I(X;U|Y)$$
for every $D\ge D_{\min}$. For $D<D_{\min}$ no code can attain the distortion. The stated single-encoder formula is exact; the multiterminal lossy statement proved separately on this page is only an inner bound.
